description:
FOUND s512p (Opus, 2026-10-08) answering #2875 (measurement there; quiet box, load ~1, best of 3, wall incl. ~0.175 s start-up, main 5adcc156):
  my $u;      for my $i (1..30000) { $u .= "line $i\n" }   perl 0.002 s   PCL 2.06 s   (in a sub: 2.53 s)
  my $u = ""; for my $i (1..30000) { $u .= "line $i\n" }   perl 0.002 s   PCL 0.23 s
  my $u; my $s = "line 12345\n"; ... $u .= $s               PCL 2.69 s (single run, load 1.8)
EMISSION: `my $u;` -> (p-let (($u :scalar (p-undef))) ... (p-.=-raw $u (p-string-concat ...))) ; `my $u = "";` -> (p-let (($u :str-buffer (%pcl-str-buffer "")))).  The str-buffer gate (Pl/Passes.pm Kind-A `str-buffer`) evidently requires a string initializer.  `my $x; $x .= ...` is how ordinary programs spell an accumulator, so this is likely the biggest cheap perf lever in output-building loops.
DIRECTION (measure first): either widen the gate to an undef initializer when every use of the cell before its first `.=` is absent / definedness is preserved (an str-buffer that remembers 'undef until first append' -- `defined $u`, `$u // "x"`, `print $u` with warnings all must read undef before the first append), or give p-.=-raw on a :scalar slot the in-place buffer the :strbuf box cell already has (the hash-element spelling is fast: 0.015 s).  Bar: a hand-replaced A/B, perl-probed definedness rows, a bench row.
subject: PERF: `my $u; $u .= ...` (a lexical declared WITHOUT an initializer) never gets the :str-buffer slot -- 30 000 appends 2.06 s vs perl 0.002 s and vs 0.05 s for `my $u = "";` -- the most common spelling of an accumulator is quadratic
